research_questions.scope: Selected US GAAP owner/developer with land acquisition, development work in progress and a separate construction contractor; 2026 reporting period; no current ASC 970 conclusion.

Paragraph 4 addresses probable, directly identifiable preacquisition costs; paragraph 7 addresses project and clearly related indirect costs; paragraphs 11-12 address allocation and periodic revision; paragraph 24 routes recoverability to FAS 144.

research_questions.answer: For the selected historical real-estate project route, FAS 67 paragraph 4 supports capitalizing qualifying directly identifiable preacquisition costs when acquisition is probable, paragraph 7 supports project costs and indirect costs clearly related to projects, paragraph 11 supplies specific-identification or relative-value allocation, paragraph 12 requires periodic review and revision, and paragraph 24 sends recoverability to FAS 144. These are historical source routes, not current ASC 970/360 conclusions. A property owner/developer ledger remains separate from a construction contractor customer contract under Topic 606.
inputs: Direct labor, materials, permits and subcontractor invoices tagged to project
Overhead allocation policy and resource-consumption basis
Entity role, intended use, sale or rental plan and current US GAAP topic
research_questions.treatment: Classify role and intended use; use FAS 67 only as the dated project-cost evidence path; separate land, qualifying preacquisition costs, project costs and clearly related indirect costs; route general overhead and costs not clearly related to a project to current-authority review rather than automatic capitalization. Keep contractor revenue analysis separate.
workflow: Freeze project population at period end
controls: Unique project ID and title evidence
Separate owner/developer and contractor role flags
exceptions: Land held for rental, sale or development may follow different current guidance. A contractor can be a related party or service provider without making the owner a contractor. Tax capitalization and local property law are outside scope.
remaining_gaps: Current consolidated Codification, later amendments, entity adoption and contract-specific facts must be checked before an accounting conclusion.

question_rows.answer: Identify the controlled asset and right to use it, then separate lease consideration, nonlease services, concession or incentive terms and refundable deposit obligations. A deposit is not rent merely because cash was received.
inputs: Identified asset, term, options and payment schedule
Deposit terms, refund conditions and tenant ledger
question_rows.treatment: Build a cents payment schedule; separately track deposit liability, lease consideration and nonlease services; reconcile concessions to the approved calculation; use current Topic 842 before posting.
workflow: Reconcile tenant balance and deposit liability
exceptions: Short-term lease, common-area service, tenant-improvement, renewal-option and variable-payment facts can change the route; this packet does not assert a low-value election.

question_rows.answer: First identify whether the transaction is a real-estate property or inventory sale, a nonfinancial-asset disposal, or a customer contract for construction or services. For a real-estate sale branch, FAS 66 paragraphs 3-6 provide dated evidence about consummation, collectibility, buyer investment, subordination and continuing involvement. FAS 67 paragraph 24 addresses recoverability for property held for development or held and used. Topic 606 is used here only for a separate customer-service or contractor branch. Current consolidated guidance and entity facts remain required.
question_rows.treatment: Hold a sale pending authorized transfer evidence and applicable topic. Reconcile contract asset, liability, deposit and recognized amount to signed terms; do not use the synthetic branch as a posting instruction.
exceptions: Installment terms, sales of units, rental property, development inventory, repurchase rights and entity-specific industry guidance may route differently.

question_rows.answer: For an equipment lessor, first classify each lease component under the dated Topic 842 route. Paragraphs 842-10-15-38 through 15-39 require a lessor to allocate consideration between lease and nonlease components using the stated allocation requirements. Paragraphs 842-30-25-1 through 25-13 provide separate recognition paths for sales-type, direct-financing and operating leases. Maintenance remains a separate service question. This is a bounded issued-update reading, not a current classification conclusion.
inputs: Lease term, options and payment schedule
question_rows.treatment: Map each contract line to a component; reconcile fixed payment and service billing separately; flag allocation judgments for current-topic review.
controls: No grossing refundable deposit into rental revenue
exceptions: Service-inclusive rental, variable usage, sale-and-leaseback, sublease, residual guarantees and specialized assets require additional review.

question_rows.answer: In the synthetic agency branch, tenant rent collected for the owner is a settlement liability while the manager recognizes only the contractually earned fee, subject to current principal-versus-agent analysis. Preserve owner funds, tenant deposits and manager revenue as separate populations.
inputs: Authority to set rent, select tenants or direct services
question_rows.treatment: For a synthetic $120,000 collection and 5% fee, reconcile $6,000 manager fee, $114,000 owner settlement liability and any separate $20,000 refundable deposit. This is a worked control example, not every manager contract.
workflow: Reconcile receipts to owner and tenant ledgers
controls: Owner remittance and deposit liability reconciliation
exceptions: A manager can control a specified service in some arrangements; a broker commission, owner-operated property and tenant security deposit can route differently. Legal fiduciary and trust rules are outside scope.
